name: Werebear
body:
Werebears are guardians of the wilderness, embodying the raw power and stoic nature of bears. With the ability to shift between different forms, these lycanthropes are revered and feared for their strength and resilience. Werebears maintain a deep connection with the natural world, often choosing to live in remote forests, mountainous regions, or other secluded natural environments where they can protect their domain from intruders and live in harmony with the land.

Unlike their more feral kin, werebears are known for their wisdom and temperance, often avoiding unnecessary conflict and showing a surprising level of control over their bestial nature. They are solitary by nature but form strong bonds with their kin and any they consider part of their “pack”.

Habitat

Werebears prefer the solitude of nature, making their homes in dense forests, secluded valleys, or hidden caves in mountainous areas. These locations allow them to live freely without the need to hide their true nature, providing ample space to roam and access to resources. Werebears take great care to protect their territory from threats, both mundane and magical, ensuring the safety of the flora and fauna within.

Strengths

The most notable strengths of werebears include their incredible physical prowess, with enhanced strength and durability that make them formidable opponents in any confrontation. Their senses are sharply honed, allowing them to track friends and foes alike through the densest woods. Werebears also possess a natural affinity for healing, able to recover from wounds at a remarkable rate and, in some tales, even heal others with their touch. Their bite carries the curse of lycanthropy, capable of transforming other creatures into werebears.

Weaknesses

Despite their many strengths, werebears are vulnerable to silver weapons, which can pierce their natural defenses. Their innate connection to nature also makes them susceptible to magical corruption or blight, which can weaken them or drive them into a frenzy. The solitary nature of werebears means they often lack allies in times of need, relying instead on their own strength and cunning to survive.

Social Structure

Werebears are loners for the most part, coming together only in times of great need or to share in the bounty of a particularly successful hunt. When they do form groups, these are usually small families or clans bound by blood or deep friendship rather than formal hierarchies. Leadership, when it exists, is based on wisdom and experience rather than dominance, with the eldest or most knowledgeable werebear guiding the others.

Interaction with Other Races

Werebears are cautious in their dealings with non-lycanthropes, preferring to observe from a distance rather than engage directly. When they do interact with outsiders, it is often in the guise of their humanoid form, using their natural charisma and wisdom to guide or dissuade those who venture too close to their territories. In rare cases, werebears have been known to form lasting friendships with non-lycanthropes, particularly druids, rangers, and others who share their deep respect for nature.

About the Curse

Becoming a werebear can often result from a deliberate act, such as seeking the blessing of a werebear elder, or through less intentional means, such as surviving an attack by a werebear in bear form. Those who inherit the curse often undergo a period of adjustment, learning to control their transformations and the urges that come with their new form. For many, the werebear curse is a call to stewardship, urging them to protect the natural world and those who live in harmony with it.

Werebear Traits

Werebears are the embodiment of strength and resilience, merging the formidable might of bears with the intelligence and form of humanoids. These lycanthropes live lives defined by a balance between their nurturing instincts and the fierce protectiveness of their bear nature. Originating from a wide array of humanoid races, werebears carry their lycanthropic traits alongside their inherent racial characteristics, leading existences that harmonize the tranquility of nature with a strong sense of community and family. Preferring remote, wild landscapes like dense forests and rugged mountains for their homes, werebears create sanctuaries that are often hidden from the prying eyes of civilization. When you play as a Werebear, you gain the following racial traits:

Ability Score Increase. Your Strength score increases by 2, and your Constitution score increases by 1.
Age. Werebears mature at the same rate as their humanoid counterparts but can live significantly longer, often attributed to their lycanthropic vitality.
Alignment. The nature of werebears leans towards good, given their protective instincts and preference for peaceful coexistence with nature. They tend toward lawful and neutral alignments, guided by a strong moral compass and a deep respect for the natural order.
Size. In humanoid form, werebears are indistinguishable from their base race. In bear or hybrid form, they become massive, often standing between 7 to 8 feet tall and weighing upwards of 400 pounds. Your size is Medium.
Speed. Your base walking speed is 30 feet. In your bear or hybrid form, you gain the ability to move through difficult terrain in forest environments without penalty.
Senses. Darkvision. Your lycanthropic heritage sharpens your senses, granting you darkvision up to 60 feet. You can see in dim light as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light, discerning shades of gray.
Languages. You can speak, read, and write Common and one other language of your choice. In bear or hybrid form, you can understand these languages but cannot speak.
Lycanthropic Resilience. You have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from attacks made with weapons that are not silvered.
Shapechanger. As an action, you can polymorph into a bear or hybrid bear form, or back into your humanoid form. While in bear or hybrid form, you retain your alignment, personality, and mental ability scores. You revert to your humanoid form if you die.
Keen Smell. You have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on smell.
Powerful Build. In your bear or hybrid form, you count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity and the weight you can push, drag, or lift.
Bite and Claw. In your bear or hybrid form, you can make a bite attack and a claw attack as part of the same action. The bite deals 1d8 + your Strength modifier in piercing damage, and the claw deals 1d6 + your Strength modifier in slashing damage.
Unstable Transformation. The physical and mental toll of transformation can leave you weakened, as detailed at page 17.
Turning

The process of transformation into a were-form after a bite is violent and painful, with the afflicted individual’s body undergoing rapid changes during the next full moon, including the growth of fur, elongation of teeth into fearsome fangs, and reshaping of the physique into a more animalistic form. For those newly cursed, the transformation is often accompanied by a complete loss of self-control, with the individual succumbing to a primal, ferocious mentality driven only by the need to hunt and survive. It’s during this initial stage that many do not survive. The stress on the body and mind is overwhelming, and without proper guidance or support, the freshly turned werewolf may perish, either due to the intensity of the transformation or through conflict with other creatures. However, some individuals manage to endure and eventually thrive with their newfound powers through their strength of will. While daunting, lycanthropy is considered by many a dark blessing. Those who survive the initial phases of the transformation find themselves imbued with heightened senses and increased physical strength. With time and practice, some werewolves even learn to wield their transformation voluntarily, utilizing their powers at their advantage.
